title: Blue Hour
description: The twenty minutes after sunset, lying on your back on the kerb of a city street: a shaft of sky walled by two towers, a crane, brick and glass, every vertical running in to the zenith. Drag across and the evening runs: the skylight falls three and a half stops while the shaft deepens from pale peach-cyan to cobalt, darkest straight overhead, the clouds lose the sun faster than the sky loses its light and sink from peach-white to a dim rose-grey, and the one sodium lamp at the bottom edge trips on its photocell and warms slowly from a dim pink strike to amber. The lamp is a real emitter cut from the HDR panorama, so its bloom and halation through the film come from its own radiance.
intent: Genre spec idea 10, Blue Hour (factory/reality/genre-spec.md section 4), after Todd Hido's dusk houses and CineStill 800T: glow that behaves like optics, as the one night-adjacent piece. Reference: https://www.toddhido.com/ and https://cinestillfilm.com/products/800tungsten-high-speed-color-film-135-36exp . ?t=0..1 holds the time (0 = sunset, 1 = twenty minutes on); ?still=1 skips the reveal.

photo.name: Grzegorz Wronkowski, Modern Evening Street (Poly Haven HDRI, CC0)

sources: HDRI: Modern Evening Street, Poly Haven, by Grzegorz Wronkowski, CC0. https://polyhaven.com/a/modern_evening_street (8k .hdr: https://dl.polyhaven.org/file/ph-assets/HDRIs/hdr/8k/modern_evening_street_8k.hdr). Rectilinear worm's-eye view, 94 deg across, the axis pitched 84 deg up at yaw 116 (between the two towers) with the frame slid 0.2 half-widths below it, so the zenith and every vertical's vanishing point sit inside the frame; rendered 2x supersampled and shipped at 1440x1800. Offline split: the sky matte (depth from Depth Anything V2 plus a two-colour luminance and chroma projection at the edges) and the one emitter in frame (a sodium lamp head) cut out as radiance above its surround, its diffraction star painted out of both layers; ambient (lights off) as log2 radiance -10..+3 in 8 bits, emitters as log2 -9..+14. The plate's own clouds were a few scraps under an equirect pole pinch, so the whole cloud layer comes from a second, sky-only HDRI through the same view (tools/depth/bakes/blue-hour/clouds.py), split by colour rather than luminance: cover is how far a pixel's blue/red ratio has fallen from the local clear sky's, light is its luminance over that clear sky ranked inside the cloud, shipped in separate channels so a puff's thin rim is never read as its grey middle. One source, no patch and no seam, so the gaps are clean sky and the zenith deepens by the radial gradient alone.

HDRI (cloud): Kloofendal 48d Partly Cloudy (Pure Sky), Poly Haven, by Greg Zaal with sky edits by Jarod Guest, CC0. https://polyhaven.com/a/kloofendal_48d_partly_cloudy_puresky (8k .hdr: https://dl.polyhaven.org/file/ph-assets/HDRIs/hdr/8k/kloofendal_48d_partly_cloudy_puresky_8k.hdr), seen through the plate's view at its own yaw: about 47% of the shaft under fair-weather cumulus, its sun just outside the frame.
